**STOP: B has to rule on A-R456-REVIEW-M1 before this round can pass.** Every step of the task went through, but the required code-reviewer found a new Medium bug in B's sketch. I reproduced it myself, and the fix is in files I'm not allowed to hand-edit.

**The finding.** The new import walker (`IMPORT_STATEMENT` in `style-scan.ts:79-80`) skips any `import` or `export … from` that has a comment inside its `{ … }`.
- **Live case:** `components/animations/index.ts` has `// Variants for custom use` inside its `export { … } from './ScrollReveal'`. So `components/animations/ScrollReveal.tsx` comes out as not mounted, although `routes/_index.tsx:39` imports it.
- **Why it's Medium:** it errs in the unsafe direction. A mounted file using a "dead" class, sitting behind such an import, would pass LT7 as unmounted.
- **Not on B's known-limits list:** TL-R455-WALKER-LIMITS lists commented-out imports, which make the walker over-count (safe). This case makes it under-count.
- **Effect today: none, measured.** Stripping comments before matching changes the result for one file only (288 → 289 files reached): ScrollReveal, which uses no dead class. None of TrackRow, WaveForm, TrackRowSkeleton or PianoLoadingAnimation becomes reachable, so LT7's current "unmounted" verdicts hold.
- **Origin:** B spec. LT7's use of the walker is new in the sketch. The regex itself is unchanged from `db95f40`, and the existing test GT5b already reads it.
- **Fix:** strip comments in the walker before matching, and add an LT8 case with a commented barrel. Both are in sha-pinned "sketch only" files, so I left the tree as it is.

**What I ran:**
- **Before applying:** claims matched B's planning output and stderr was empty. The sketch and file checksums were OK, `git apply` was clean, and I made no hand edits.
- **Docs:**
  - Doc 298: only line 4 changed, now `**სტატუსი:** Completed (C round 455 PASS)`.
  - Doc 299: new, line 4 in the stage form the task gives, the seven template headings in order, no "pending", and every LT/GS id it cites exists in the tests.
  - Doc 299 still says "C round 456 PASS" as the task requires, and its walker sentence overstates what the walker does. B should rule on both.
- **Checks:**
  - `npm run typecheck`: passes.
  - `npm run lint`: 205 warnings, the same as at HEAD.
  - Biome on the three test files: passes, no fixes.
  - Covering set: 4 files / 26 tests pass.
- **Mutants:** run on a separate scratch copy, not the store tree. The output is identical to B's: BASE and C1 pass, M1–M20 fail as expected.
- **After the changes:** claims match the sketch output except K2 and K10, which differ as expected; stderr empty. `git status` shows exactly the 5 granted paths, re-checked after the probes.

I did not run the full test suite, the build or `npm run verify`; those belong to the root gate. I did no browser work. I read the pre-flight skill late, after applying the sketch, and the report says so.

**Other reviewer notes:**
- **Two Lows:** `ImportBinding.exported` holds the local alias name on imports; `cssRuleBodies` and `cssRuleSelectorCount` match selectors differently, which their names don't show.
- **Architecture note for B/root:** `style-scan.ts` now holds two separate parts, the CSS rule reader and the import walker. This is already requested as ARCH-CHECKPOINT-STYLE-SCAN. I did not act on it.

**For C:** go straight to the short route, since B hasn't ruled yet. Run C1, C2 and the C7 purchase guard, then my probe on a scratch clone, then write a short FAIL routed to B. The full C1–C9 list applies only if B re-dispatches.

Everything is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/`:
- `a-round-456.md` (the report)
- `a-round-456/` (logs, mutants, claims)
- `a-round-456/probe/` (the probe test `zz-flip-probe.test.ts`, its usage note and `flip-probe.log`)
